description:
REPORTED BY USER, 2026-09-12, while verifying T-001/T-005: "When it is down we should have a flag that says API is down. We should be detecting that asap since nothing is loading."

T-001 gave every MUTATION a failure banner. QUERIES still fail silently: TanStack retries once, then the screen sits on its loading or empty state with no explanation. After T-005 you are no longer ejected to sign-in when the API is down — which is correct, but it means you now sit on an app that renders and never fills, with nothing saying why. T-005 traded a wrong answer for no answer; this ticket supplies the answer.

WANTED: one app-level indicator that the API cannot be reached, raised as early as possible, cleared automatically when it comes back.

DESIGN NOTES (verified against the code, 2026-09-12):
- `/health` exists at `apps/api/src/index.ts:58` but is mounted at the ROOT, not under `/api`. `apps/web/vite.config.ts` proxies ONLY `/api`, and `env.apiUrl` is "" in dev, so a browser probe of `/health` in dev hits the Vite dev server rather than the API. Either add `/health` to the Vite proxy or move the endpoint under `/api`. Do not assume a probe path works in both environments without checking — dev and prod resolve it differently.
- Earliest available signal is the route guard: `checkSession` (`lib/auth/session-check.ts`) runs on EVERY in-app navigation and already distinguishes "could not ask" from "signed out". An unanswered check is the first evidence the API is gone, and it happens before any screen query is issued.
- Second signal is query/mutation failure. `lib/query/query-client.ts` currently passes no `QueryCache`/`MutationCache`, so there is no global hook; adding `new QueryCache({ onError, onSuccess })` gives one place to observe every request outcome without touching call sites.
- Distinguish "never reached the server" from "server answered badly". `ApiError` is only constructed from a real response (`lib/api/client.ts:39`), so anything that is NOT an ApiError is a transport failure. Consider whether 502/503/504 should count as unreachable too — on Cloud Run a cold-start failure surfaces that way.
- Recovery must be automatic: poll while down, and on success invalidate queries so screens refill without a reload. Do not poll while healthy.
- Placement: the root route component covers the sign-in screen too, which AppLayout does not — and the sign-in screen is exactly where someone lands when the API is down.

RELATED: T-001 (mutation failures, done), T-005 (auth check survives an unreachable API, done), ISS-001 (no optimistic updates).
title: Say when the API is unreachable instead of showing empty screens
